source_text: Qui vero non hic, id est, non intra hunc ambitum terrae, nec per hunc commeatum vitae, nec apud homines hujus naturae communis confessionem putant constitutam, quanta praesumptio est adversus omnem ordinem rerum in terris istis, et in vita ista, et sub humanis potestatibus experiundarum? Nimirum cum animae de corporibus excesserint, et per singula tabulata coelorum de praecepto dispici coeperint, et interrogari arcana illa haereticorum sacramenta, tunc confitendum apud veras potestates et veros homines, Theletos scilicet et Abascantos et Acinetos Valentini. Nostrates enim, inquiunt, nec ipse Demiurgus constanter homines probabat veros esse, quos stillicidium situlae et pulverem areae et sputamen et locustas deputavit; etiam irrationalibus jumentis adaequavit. Plane ita scriptum. Non tamen idcirco aliud hominis genus intelligendum praeter nos: quos quia constat esse, et comparatione potuit induere, salva et proprietate generis, et singularitate. Neque enim si vita vitiata est, ut despectui judicata despectis compararetur, statim natura sublata est, ut alia in nomine ejus deputaretur. Atquin servatur natura, etsi suffunditur vita, nec alios novit Christus homines, quam de quibus dicit: Quem me aiunt esse homines? et: Quomodo vultis ut faciant vobis homines, et ita vos facite illis. Vide an servaverit genus, a quibus et testimonium sui exspectet, et in quos justitiae vicem mandat. Illos autem coelestes homines si expostulem mihi ostendi, facilius Aratus Persea, et Cephea, et Erigonam, et Ariadnam inter sidera deliniabit. Quis autem prohibuit Dominum illic etiam confessionem hominum faciendam manifeste determinare, ubi suam futuram aperte pronuntiavit? ut ita esset positum: «Qui in me confessus fuerit coram hominibus in coelis, et ego in illo confitebor coram Patre meo qui in coelis est?» Eripere me debuit ex isto terrenae confessionis errore, quam suscipi noluit, si coelestem praecepisset, quia nullos alios homines noveram praeter incolas terrae; ne ipso quidem adhuc tunc in coelis homine conspecto. Quae porro fides rerum, ut post excessum ad superna sublevatus, illic probarer, quo non nisi jam probatus imponerer? illic de praecepto examinarer, quo nisi admittendus pervenire non possem? Christiano coelum ante patet quam via; quia nulla via in coelum, nisi cui patet coelum; quod qui attigerit, intrabit. Quas mihi potestates janitrices affirmas juxta romanam superstitionem Janum quemdam et Forculum et Limentinum? quas a cancellis ordinas potestates? Si unquam legisti apud David, auferte portas principes vestras, et subleventur portae aeternae, et intrabit rex gloriae. Si item audisti apud Amos: Qui assensum illum suum aedificat in coelos, et profusionem suam fundat in terras; scito et ascensum illum exinde complanatum vestigiis Domini, et introitum exinde reseratum viribus Christi, nec ullam moram aut quaestionem in limine Christianis occursuram, qui non dignosci habeant illic, sed agnosci; nec interrogari, sed admitti. Nam et si adhuc clausum putas coelum, memento claves ejus hic Dominum Petro, et per eum, Ecclesiae reliquisse, quas hic unusquisque interrogatus atque confessus feret secum. Sed asseverat diabolus illic confitendum, ut suadeat hic negandum. Pulchra videlicet documenta praemittam, bonas mecum claves feram, timorem eorum, qui solum corpus occidunt, animae autem nihil faciunt: commendatus ero hujus praecepti desertione; honeste in coelestibus stabo, qui in terrenis stare non potui; sustinebo majores potestates, qui minoribus cessi; merebor denique admitti, jam exclusus. Suppetit adhuc dicere: si in coelestibus confitendum, et hic negandum est; nam ubi alterum, ibi utrumque; aemula enim quaeque concurrunt. Etiam persecutionem in coelis agitari oportebit, quae confessionis negationisve materia est. Quid itaque cessas, audacissime haeretice, totum ordinem christianae concussionis in superna transferre, et in primis, ipsum nominis odium illic collocare, ubi ad Patris dexteram praesidet Christus? Illic constitues et synagogas Judaeorum, fontes persecutionum, apud quas Apostoli flagella perpessi sunt, et populos nationum cum suo quidem circo, ubi facile conclamant, «Usquequo genus tertium?» Sed et fratres nostros et patres et filios et socrus et nurus et domesticos nostros ibidem exhibere debebis, per quos traditio disposita est: item reges et praesides et armatas potestates, apud quos caussa purganda est. Erit certe etiam carcer in coelo, carens sole, aut ingratis luminosus, et vincula fortasse de zonis, et equuleus axis ipse qui torquet: tum si lapidandus christianus, grandines aderunt; si urendus, fulmina prae manu sunt; si trucidandus, Orionis armati manus operabitur; si bestiis finiendus, ursas septemtrio emittet, zodiacus tauros et leones. Haec qui sustinuerit in finem, iste erit salvus. Ergone et finis in coelis, et passio, et occisio, et prima confessio? Et ubi caro, omnibus istis necessaria? ubi corpus? quod solum ab hominibus habet occidi. Haec nobis etiam ludicrum in modum certa ratio mandavit, nec ullus obicem praescriptionis istius extrudet, ut non omnem ordinem persecutionis, omnem ejus caussae firmam paraturam illuc transferre cogatur, ubi confessioni forum dederit. Siquidem confessio a persecutione deducitur, et persecutio in confessione finitur. Nec possunt non una sequi, quae et aditum et exitum, id est, initium finemque disponunt. Porro et odium nominis hic erit, et persecutio hic erumpit, et traditio hic producit, et interrogatio hic compellit, et carnificina hic desaevit, et totum hunc ordinem in terris confessio vel negatio expungit. Igitur si caetera hic, nec confessio alibi; si confessio alibi, nec caetera hic. Enimvero non alibi caetera; itaque nec confessio in coelo. Aut si aliam volunt esse rationem interrogationis et confessionis coelestis, utique et ordinem suum illi struere debebunt alium longe, et ab ista dispositione diversum, quae Scripturis notatur, et possumus dicere, Viderint, dum hic ordo terrenae interrogationis et confessionis, ex materia decurrens persecutionis et discordiae publicae in nomen, salvus sit suae fidei; ut ita credendum sit sicut et scribitur, ita intelligendum sit sicuti auditur. Hic omnem ordinem sustineo, ipso Domino non aliam regionem mundi destinante. Quid enim post confessionis et negationis terminum subjungit? Ne putaveritis venisse me uti pacem mittam in terram; non veni, sed ut machaeram, certe in terram. Veni enim dividere hominem adversus patrem suum, et filiam adversus matrem suam, et socrum adversus nurum suam: et inimici homini domestici sui. Sic enim efficitur, ut tradat frater fratrem in mortem, et pater filium, et insurgant filii in parentes, et mori eos faciant. Et qui sustinuerit in finem, hic salvus erit. Adeo totus hic ordo dominicae machaerae, non in coelum missae, sed in terram, illic constituit etiam confessionem, quae in finem sustinendo passura est mortem.
pass_a_gloss: But truly, those who do not think that the common confession of this nature is established here, that is, not within this circle of the earth, nor through this journey of life, nor among men, what a great presumption it is against all order of things on this earth and in this life and under human powers to be experienced? Doubtless, when souls have departed from bodies and have begun to be examined by command through the individual levels of the heavens and to be questioned about those secret sacraments of the heretics, then it will be necessary to confess among the true powers and true men, namely Theletos and Abascantos and Acinetos of Valentinus. For our people, they say, not even the Demiurgus himself consistently proved men to be true, whom he assigned to be like the dripping of a jar and the dust of a threshing floor and spittle and locusts; he also equated them with irrational beasts. It is written plainly. Nevertheless, it is not therefore to be understood that there is another kind of men beyond us, whom, because it is agreed that they exist, and by comparison it was able to induce, with the property of the kind and the singularity being preserved. For even if life is corrupted, so that it may be judged to be despised and compared to the despised, the nature is not immediately abolished, so that another may be appointed in its name. But the nature is preserved, even if life is corrupted, and Christ does not know any other men than those about whom he says: 'What do men say that I am?' and 'How do you want men to do to you, and so you do to them.' See whether he has preserved the kind, from whom he also expects testimony of himself, and in whom he commands the turn of justice. But if I were to ask to be shown those heavenly men, Aratus would more easily depict Perseus and Cepheus and Erigone and Ariadne among the stars. Who, however, prevented the Lord from determining there also that a confession of men should be made manifestly, where he openly proclaimed his future, so that it would be established: 'Whoever has confessed me before men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven?' He ought to have rescued me from this error of earthly confession, which he did not want to receive, if he had commanded a heavenly one, because I knew no other men except the inhabitants of the earth; not even the man in heaven was seen by me at that time. What faith is there in things, so that after passing away, being elevated to the things above, I may be approved there, to which I could not be brought unless already approved? There I would be examined by command, to which I could not arrive unless admitted? For the Christian, heaven lies open before the way; because there is no way to heaven, unless heaven lies open; which whoever has touched, will enter. What gatekeeper powers do you affirm to me, according to the Roman superstition, some Janus and Forculus and Limentinus? What powers do you arrange at the gates? If you have ever read in David, 'Remove your gates, princes, and the eternal gates will be lifted up, and the king of glory will enter,' and also if you have heard in Amos: 'Who builds his ascent to the heavens and founds his abundance on the earth; know that his ascent from there is made smooth by the footsteps of the Lord, and his entrance from there is opened by the powers of Christ,' and no delay or questioning will occur to Christians at the threshold, who will not be distinguished there, but recognized; nor questioned, but admitted. For even if you still think that heaven is closed, remember that the Lord left its keys here to Peter, and through him, to the rest of the Church, which each one, having been questioned and confessed, will carry with him. But the devil asserts that one must confess there, so that he may persuade to deny here. I will certainly bring forth beautiful documents, I will carry good keys with me, the fear of those who can only kill the body, but do nothing to the soul; I will be commended by the abandonment of this command; I will stand honorably in the heavenly places, who was not able to stand on earth; I will endure greater powers, who yielded to lesser ones; I will finally deserve to be admitted, now being excluded. It is still possible to say: if one must confess in heaven, and deny here; for where one is, the other is also; for rival things run together. Also, persecution must be stirred up in heaven, which is the material for confession or denial. Why, therefore, do you hesitate, most audacious heretic, to transfer the entire order of Christian agitation to the things above, and first of all, to place the hatred of the name there, where Christ presides at the right hand of the Father? There you will establish the synagogues of the Jews, the sources of persecutions, among which the apostles suffered lashes, and the peoples of the nations with their own circus, where they easily cry out, 'How long until the third kind?' But you must also exhibit our brothers and fathers and sons and mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law and our household members there, through whom the tradition is arranged; also kings and rulers and armed powers, among whom the case is to be purified. There will certainly also be a prison in heaven, lacking the sun, or shining with unpleasant light, and chains perhaps made of straps, and a rack which is the axis itself that twists; then if a Christian is to be stoned, hailstones will be at hand; if he is to be burned, lightning will be before him; if he is to be killed, the armed hands of Orion will work; if he is to be finished by beasts, the seven stars will send out bears, the zodiac will send out bulls and lions. He who will have endured these things to the end will be saved. Is it therefore also the end and passion and killing and first confession in heaven? And where is the flesh, necessary for all these things? Where is the body, which alone can be killed by men? This certain reason has commanded us, and no one will push away the objection of this prescription, so that it is not necessary to transfer the entire order of persecution, the entire firm preparation of its case, to the place where he has given a forum to confession. Since confession is derived from persecution, and persecution ends in confession, they cannot but follow one another, which arrange both the beginning and the end, that is, the entrance and exit. Furthermore, the hatred of the name will be here, and persecution will break out here, and tradition will produce here, and questioning will compel here, and carnage will rage here, and the entire order of confession or denial will be destroyed on earth. Therefore, if the other things are here, confession is not elsewhere; if confession is elsewhere, the other things are not here. For the other things are not elsewhere; therefore, confession is not in heaven. But if they want to be another reason for heavenly questioning and confession, they will certainly have to construct another order for it, far different and diverse from this arrangement, which is noted in the Scriptures, and we can say, 'Let them see to it,' as long as this order of earthly questioning and confession, flowing from the material of persecution and public discord in the name, is preserved in its faith; so that it is to be believed as it is written, and understood as it is heard. I sustain the entire order here, the Lord himself not appointing another region of the world. What, therefore, does he add after the limit of confession and denial? 'Do not think that I have come to bring peace on earth; I have not come, but to bring a sword, certainly on earth.' For I have come to divide a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law; and a man's enemies will be those of his own household. For thus it happens that a brother hands over a brother to death, and a father his son, and sons rise up against their parents, and make them die. And he who will have endured to the end will be saved. So the entire order of the Lord's sword is not sent to heaven, but to earth, and establishes confession there, which will suffer death by enduring to the end.

pass_b_english: What's the point of thinking that our common confession isn't established here on earth, in this life, and among humans? That's a huge presumption against the natural order of things. When we die and our souls are examined level by level in the heavens, and we're questioned about the secret sacraments of heretics, we'll have to confess to the true powers and true men - Theletos, Abascantos, and Acinetos, according to Valentinus. Our people say that not even the Demiurgus consistently proved humans to be true, comparing us to things like dripping water, dust, and spittle, and even equating us with irrational animals (Matthew 10:32-33). It's written plainly, but that doesn't mean there's another kind of human beyond us. If life is corrupted, that doesn't mean our nature is abolished. Christ knows us, and he says, 'What do people say that I am?' and 'Do to others what you want them to do to you' (Matthew 10:32-33). He preserves our kind, expecting testimony from us and commanding us to turn to justice. If I asked to see these heavenly men, it would be easier to point out constellations like Perseus and Cepheus. Who stopped the Lord from making it clear that we should confess our faith openly, just like he proclaimed his future, saying, 'Whoever confesses me before others, I will confess them before my Father in heaven' (Matthew 10:32-33)? He should have rescued me from this earthly confession if he wanted a heavenly one, but I only know of humans on earth. What's the point of being approved in heaven if we're already approved on earth? The Christian path to heaven is open, but only if heaven is open to us - and if we touch it, we'll enter. What gatekeeper powers are you talking about, like Janus and Forculus from Roman superstition? The Lord left the keys to heaven with Peter and the Church, and we'll carry them with us when we're questioned and confessed. The devil says we must confess in heaven to persuade us to deny our faith on earth. But if we must confess in heaven, why not also persecute and deny on earth? It's all connected - if one happens, so does the other. Why hesitate to transfer the entire Christian struggle to heaven, including the hatred of our name, when Christ is at the right hand of the Father? You'd have to establish the synagogues of the Jews, the sources of persecution, and the nations with their circuses, all over again. And what about our families and household members, through whom tradition is passed down? There would have to be kings, rulers, and armed powers to judge our case. And a prison in heaven, with chains and a rack, where Christians could be stoned, burned, or killed by beasts. Whoever endures to the end will be saved, but is that really how it works in heaven? Where's the flesh and body needed for all that? The Lord didn't come to bring peace on earth but a sword, to divide us against each other, so that a brother might hand over a brother to death, and a father his son (Matthew 10:34-36). The entire order of the Lord's sword is on earth, not in heaven, and it's here that we must confess and endure to the end. As the Psalm says, 'Lift up your heads, O gates, and the King of glory will come in' (Psalm 24:7,9), and Amos says, 'Who builds his ascent to the heavens...?' (Amos 9:6). We can't push away the fact that confession and persecution are connected, and that our faith is preserved in the order of things on earth, not in some heavenly realm.
